lines.text: Many learners say: I asked from my teacher to help me.
Better: I asked my teacher to help me.
Ask needs no from before a person.
My! I asked my friend for help.

data.wrong: I asked from my teacher to help me.
data.right: I asked my teacher to help me.
data.why: Ask needs no from before a person.

native.tip: نترجم «طلبتُ من معلمي» حرفيًا، لكن ask يأخذ الشخص بلا from: “I asked my teacher to help me.” وليس “I asked from my teacher.”
native.caption: هل تقول أحيانًا هذه الجملة؟ “I asked from my teacher to help me.” 😅 مع ask نذكر الشخص مباشرةً بلا from، فالجملة الصحيحة “I asked my teacher to help me.” استمع إلى Ama وكرّر! تدرّب أكثر في تطبيق Lexkite.
native.comment: الإجابة: “my” — مع ask نذكر الشخص مباشرةً بلا from. اختبار مجاني هنا: {link}
native.ncap: مع ask نذكر الشخص مباشرةً بلا from

en.tip: Ask takes the person directly, with no from: “I asked my teacher to help me.” not “I asked from my teacher to help me.”
en.caption: Do you sometimes say this? “I asked from my teacher to help me.” 😅 In English ask needs no from before a person, so the right sentence is “I asked my teacher to help me.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
